messages:
alex_chang: Heads-up — I pulled the April invoice and there's ~$18k in GPU spend in us-west1 that doesn't have cost_center labels. Strange spike, looks like orphaned reserved instances or untagged VMs. :eyes:

maya_patel: ugh. do you see if those map to any Dedicated pools or Private deploys?

alex_chang: Quick scan: most of the lines are SKUs matching nvidia-t4 and a mix of preemptible/standard. billing export rows show project = redwood-inference-prod, but label.cost_center is NULL for ~95% of those rows.

liam_rivera: could be onboarding scripts that didn't apply labels on node creation. we've had a couple of manual k8s node pools created during the last capacity migration.

olivia_ops: tagging enforcement exists in IaC for new clusters but we excluded some legacy pools. I'm worried CUD/CUD-commit utilization is attributed to billing account level and not split by product. That makes chargeback hard.

billing-bot: invoice_alert: Detached GPU spend detected for billing_account: BA-9876. Unlabeled cost = $17,942. Suggested actions: run label sweep, attach commit allocation, patch IaC.

maya_patel: Action plan: (1) find orphaned compute instances/node pools, (2) try to retro-label where possible, (3) update billing export mapping and PR to enforce labels at creation, (4) run a one-off chargeback recalculation.

liam_rivera: For step 1, run this BigQuery to get candidates (from our billing export):
```
SELECT project.id, sku.description, resource.labels, cost, usage_start_time
FROM `redwood-billing.bq_export.gcp_billing_export_v1_*`
WHERE sku.description LIKE '%GPU%'
  AND resource.labels.cost_center IS NULL
  AND invoice_month = '2026-04'
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

alex_chang: Thanks. I'll run and then correlate with GCP node metadata API to see which VM instances still exist. If they're gone, we need to tag chargebacks to the owning product by mapping project to product owner.

olivia_ops: We should also check our commitment utilization: some of these costs might be residual from CUDs that were applied at org level. If so, they should be re-allocated to teams proportionally. Erin on finance had a script for apportioning commitments — pinging her next.

maya_patel: If we can retro-label billing export rows? I don't think GCP allows rewriting historical labels — only resource labels. But we can record a mapping table for chargeback and apply to the month-end report. That's what we did after the last provider migration.

liam_rivera: Agreed. For automation: add a pre-provision hook in terraform module to require `labels = { cost_center = var.cost_center }` and fail CI if missing. Also add a nightly job to detect unlabeled resources and open tickets.

alex_chang: I found 7 node pools created in the migration window with no labels. Three are empty (terminated), four still have running pods. I'm going to add labels where possible and annotate the PR with the mapping for chargeback.

billing-bot: note: For retroactive chargeback, please add entries to `gs://redwood-billing/chargeback/2026-04/mapping.csv` with columns (resource, product, cost_center, manual_adjustment).

olivia_ops: I'll take ownership of the mapping CSV and run the finance apportionment script after the labels/mapping are final. We should also evaluate whether to move some of the spend into a Dedicated reserved pool to reduce unit cost next quarter.

maya_patel: Sounds good. Postmortem checklist: root cause = legacy manual node pools + no enforceable IaC guardrails; mitigation = retro-label/mapping + chargeback run; follow-up = terraform pre-commit checks + nightly unlabeled alert.

liam_rivera: I'll open the IaC PR and the alerting ticket. tagging sweep + mapping target EOD tomorrow. :hammer:

alex_chang: thanks team. Assigning owners: alex = run BQ/correlate, liam = IaC PR + alert, olivia = mapping + finance handoff, maya = chargeback report. Will update thread with results. :thumbsup:
